items.label: f04-zero-charge-ids
items.back: gift_<code> when a gift card covers the whole total; free_<order#> when discounts reduce the total to zero. Both skip the gateway and are real Paid orders.

items.label: f01-checkout-phases
items.front: Agora checkout: the three phases and what a decline undoes
items.back: Validate side-effect free; reserve stock and persist the Pending order in one save; charge total minus gift-card tender. Decline: release reservations, delete the order, keep cart and gift card (402). Approve: redeem card, MarkPaid, commit reservations, register discount, clear active lines (201).

items.label: f03-token-rows
items.front: Which Agora rows carry an int Version concurrency token, and why only those?
items.back: InventoryItem, Cart and GiftCard: a lost update there costs money or goods. Admin config (products, discounts, shipping, tax, webhooks) has none; a lost update there means the second edit won.

items.label: f02-totals-order
items.front: Agora totals order, from subtotal to gateway charge
items.back: discount (clamped) -> discountedSubtotal -> tax per line on the prorated discounted amount -> shipping on the discounted subtotal -> total -> giftCardTender = min(balance, total) -> gatewayCharge = total - tender.

items.prompt: An order of 3 units has one shipment covering 2 of them. An admin then cancels it. What happens?

choices.text: A 409, because Cancel accepts only Pending or Paid orders
A 200, and the 1 unshipped unit goes back into stock
A 422 Invalid fulfillment, since a shipment exists
A 200, and the order becomes Refunded instead

choices: A 409, because Cancel accepts only Pending or Paid orders
A 200, and the 1 unshipped unit goes back into stock
A 422 Invalid fulfillment, since a shipment exists
A 200, and the order becomes Refunded instead

items.explanation: The order is PartiallyFulfilled. Order.Cancel throws InvalidOrderStateException outside Pending/Paid, which maps to 409; the escape hatch is a refund.

items.prompt: A fixed-amount discount code worth 80.00 is applied to a cart whose subtotal is 50.00. What DiscountAmount is stored on the order?

choices.text: 0.00, because an oversized discount is ignored entirely
Nothing is stored: checkout rejects the code with a 422
80.00, and Subtract then clamps the discounted subtotal at zero
50.00, as CalculateDiscount caps a fixed amount at the subtotal

choices: 0.00, because an oversized discount is ignored entirely
Nothing is stored: checkout rejects the code with a 422
80.00, and Subtract then clamps the discounted subtotal at zero
50.00, as CalculateDiscount caps a fixed amount at the subtotal

items.explanation: DiscountCode.CalculateDiscount returns new Money(Math.Min(Value, subtotal.Amount)) for FixedAmount, so the stored discount is the subtotal; Subtract would clamp too, but it never has to.

items.prompt: The payment gateway declines a checkout after the Pending order was saved. What is the state afterwards?

choices.text: Reservations are released and the Pending order is deleted
Stock stays reserved and the cart lines are removed
The Pending order stays so the customer can retry payment
The gift card is redeemed, then credited back by a refund

choices: Reservations are released and the Pending order is deleted
Stock stays reserved and the cart lines are removed
The Pending order stays so the customer can retry payment
The gift card is redeemed, then credited back by a refund

items.explanation: On !payment.Success the service calls ReleaseReservation per line, removes the order and saves, then throws PaymentFailedException (402). The cart and the gift card are untouched.

items.prompt: A code has UsageLimit 1 and TimesUsed 0. Two checkouts with no products in common load it before either saves. What does the code allow?

choices.text: The second gets a 409, from a Version check on the discount code row
The unique index on Code makes the second update fail
The second gets a 422 when RegisterUse re-checks the usage limit
Both succeed, and TimesUsed ends at 1 with no token on DiscountCode

choices: The second gets a 409, from a Version check on the discount code row
The unique index on Code makes the second update fail
The second gets a 422 when RegisterUse re-checks the usage limit
Both succeed, and TimesUsed ends at 1 with no token on DiscountCode

items.explanation: Only InventoryItem, Cart and GiftCard carry Version tokens. RegisterUse checks the limit against each context's own stale TimesUsed (0), and both UPDATEs write 1, so the single-use code is used twice. The ADR treats discounts as survivable admin config; this lost update is the cost.

items.prompt: A shipping method ships free at 50.00 or more. The cart subtotal is 60.00 and a 20% code applies. What shipping is charged?

choices.text: Half the normal rate, prorated by the discount
The normal rate, because 48.00 is below the threshold
Free shipping; the threshold is checked before discounts run
Free shipping, since the 60.00 subtotal clears the threshold

choices: Half the normal rate, prorated by the discount
The normal rate, because 48.00 is below the threshold
Free shipping; the threshold is checked before discounts run
Free shipping, since the 60.00 subtotal clears the threshold

items.explanation: CalculateCharge receives the discounted subtotal (60.00 - 12.00 = 48.00) and ships free only when it is >= FreeThreshold; 48.00 is not, so BaseRate applies.

items.prompt: The process dies after the gateway approves a charge but before the final SaveChangesAsync. What state is left behind?

choices.text: The reservation rolls back, because one transaction wraps the whole request
The order reads Paid, because MarkPaid ran before the charge
A sweeper releases the reserved units once a timeout has passed
Units stay reserved and the order stays Pending; nothing expires them

choices: The reservation rolls back, because one transaction wraps the whole request
The order reads Paid, because MarkPaid ran before the charge
A sweeper releases the reserved units once a timeout has passed
Units stay reserved and the order stays Pending; nothing expires them

items.explanation: Checkout uses two separate SaveChangesAsync calls with no wrapping transaction. The first persisted the reservations and the Pending order; the ADR says no sweeper expires stale reservations.

items.prompt: Suppose TaxZoneRate.Rate lost its per-property override and fell back to the global decimal convention. What would a saved rate of 0.095 read back as?

choices.text: 0.09, since the converter truncates toward zero
0.095, because the cents converter keeps 3 decimal places
0.10, so orders in that zone are taxed at 10%
An error: SQLite rejects decimals with more than two places

choices: 0.09, since the converter truncates toward zero
0.095, because the cents converter keeps 3 decimal places
0.10, so orders in that zone are taxed at 10%
An error: SQLite rejects decimals with more than two places

items.explanation: DecimalToCentsConverter stores Math.Round(v * 100, AwayFromZero): 9.5 rounds to 10, which reads back as 0.10. That is why the rate columns opt out to millionths.

items.prompt: Two checkouts both read the last unit before either saves, so both pass Reserve. What does the slower writer get?

choices.text: A 500, because the concurrency exception is not mapped
A 201; the last write wins and the one unit is sold twice
A 409 titled Concurrency conflict, via DbUpdateConcurrencyException
A 409 titled Insufficient stock, thrown by the Reserve guard

choices: A 500, because the concurrency exception is not mapped
A 201; the last write wins and the one unit is sold twice
A 409 titled Concurrency conflict, via DbUpdateConcurrencyException
A 409 titled Insufficient stock, thrown by the Reserve guard

items.explanation: Each Reserve passed on its own snapshot. InventoryItem.Version is a concurrency token, so the second UPDATE matches 0 rows, EF throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException and the filter maps it to 409 "Concurrency conflict".

items.prompt: A gift card with a 200.00 balance pays for an order whose total is 120.00. What happens with the payment gateway?

choices.text: It is charged 120.00 and the card balance is untouched
It is charged 0.00 and its returned id is stored on the order
It is not called; the transaction id is gift_ plus the card code
It is skipped, and the transaction id is free_ plus the order number

choices: It is charged 120.00 and the card balance is untouched
It is charged 0.00 and its returned id is stored on the order
It is not called; the transaction id is gift_ plus the card code
It is skipped, and the transaction id is free_ plus the order number

items.explanation: chargeAmount is total minus min(balance, total) = 0, so ChargeAsync is skipped; with a gift card present the id is gift_<code>. free_<order#> is for a zero total with no gift card.

items.prompt: In WebhookService.DispatchAsync, when are the WebhookDelivery rows saved relative to the HTTP sends?

choices.text: Only failed deliveries are saved; successes are not written
Inside the checkout's own save, as one shared transaction
After the loop sends them, in a single SaveChangesAsync
Before any send, so that a crash leaves Pending rows to retry

choices: Only failed deliveries are saved; successes are not written
Inside the checkout's own save, as one shared transaction
After the loop sends them, in a single SaveChangesAsync
Before any send, so that a crash leaves Pending rows to retry

items.explanation: Each delivery is sent, its attempt recorded and the row added; a single SaveChangesAsync follows the loop. A crash mid-dispatch loses the log: at-most-once, as the ADR says.

items.prompt: A guest requests a return for a real order number but gives a different email than the order's. What status comes back?

choices.text: 401, because every return needs a signed-in account
403, because the caller is known but is not the order's owner
404, so the endpoint never confirms that the order exists
422; the email counts as an unknown reference

choices: 401, because every return needs a signed-in account
403, because the caller is known but is not the order's owner
404, so the endpoint never confirms that the order exists
422; the email counts as an unknown reference

items.explanation: EnsureRequesterOwnsOrder accepts a matching CustomerId or the order email (case-insensitive) and otherwise throws NotFoundException, which maps to 404.

items.prompt: An admin retries a failed webhook delivery. What does the receiver get on that retry?

choices.text: A new delivery row with its own id and attempt count of 1
A re-serialized payload; fresh createdAt and a new signature
The stored payload and stored signature, resent byte for byte
The same payload, re-signed with the current subscription secret

choices: A new delivery row with its own id and attempt count of 1
A re-serialized payload; fresh createdAt and a new signature
The stored payload and stored signature, resent byte for byte
The same payload, re-signed with the current subscription secret

items.explanation: RetryAsync sends delivery.Payload and delivery.Signature as stored and records the attempt on the same row. Nothing is re-serialized or re-signed.
